climate.overview_html: With COP31 opening in Antalya on 9 November — 20 days away — the European Parliament’s plenary session (19–22 October) is voting this week on a resolution urging the EU to lead fossil-fuel phase-out negotiations and demanding adaptation finance triple by 2035. The scientific backdrop darkens further: NOAA’s 15 October 2026–27 Winter Outlook flags a >90% probability that the super El Niño persists through January–March 2027, locking in a warm-north / wet-south US pattern. Meanwhile, an “Inside Track” whistleblower memo published 14 October alleges that catastrophe modellers and actuaries at some European insurers are being told to apply a “haircut” to forward-looking climate projections to protect commercial interests — a structurally significant claim given that reinsurance property-catastrophe rates have fallen 28% cumulatively over 2026 while physical risk is at all-time highs.

items.headline: NOAA 2026–27 Winter Outlook: Super El Niño Gives >90% Odds of Persistence Through January–March 2027; Northern US Warmer Than Average; South and Southwest Wetter Than Average
items.summary: NOAA's Climate Prediction Center released its official 2026–27 Winter Outlook on October 15, placing greater than 90% probability on the current super El Niño persisting through January–March 2027. The outlook favors warmer-than-average temperatures across the northern tier, Midwest, most of the East, and Pacific Northwest — with the Southern Rockies the primary 'Equal Chances' zone. The wet signal is strongest from Southern California, Arizona and New Mexico eastward through Texas, the Gulf Coast and Southeast. Parts of the Northwest, northern Rockies and northern Plains lean drier-than-average. NOAA's CPC put El Niño persistence probability above 83% through the three-month peak season. The full Winter Outlook is scheduled for a more detailed release around November 19.

items.headline: EU Parliament Plenary Votes This Week (19–22 Oct) on COP31 Resolution: Demands EU Lead Fossil-Fuel Phase-Out Treaty Negotiations, Adaptation Finance Triple by 2035, and Binding Fossil-Fuel Subsidy Phase-Out Timeline
items.summary: The European Parliament's full plenary session opened October 19 and is voting this week on a resolution setting Parliament's COP31 priorities. The Environment Committee passed the draft by 50 votes to 16 on October 1, demanding: (1) the EU advocate for a fossil fuel non-proliferation treaty within UNFCCC; (2) adaptation finance triple by 2035; (3) time-bound plans to phase out fossil fuel subsidies and production; (4) full operationalisation of the NCQG agreed at COP29. The draft also notes preliminary data showing EU emissions rose by 1% from 2024 to 2025. A 15-member delegation led by Environment Committee chair Lídia Pereira will attend COP31 in Antalya.

items.headline: “Sounding the Alarm” Whistleblower Memo: Senior European Insurance Insiders Allege Catastrophe Modellers Pressured to Apply “Haircut” to Climate Projections to Protect Commercial Interests
items.summary: A memo titled 'Sounding the Alarm', published October 14 by the UK non-profit Inside Track (which anonymises industry insiders), alleges that catastrophe modellers and actuaries at some European insurers and reinsurers are being pressured to lower forward-looking climate risk projections — specifically applying a 'haircut' to estimates so as not to alarm underwriters or clients. The anonymous authors are described as current and recently departed senior figures from UK and European non-life, reinsurance and broking markets. The memo warns of a three-stage industry retreat from climate-exposed risk: repricing, narrowing of cover, then withdrawal — comparing potential uninsured property exposure to the 'next sub-prime problem.' The memo also alleges that some carriers' catastrophe models rely on inadequate or outdated physical-risk scenarios and fail to capture tipping-point non-linearities.

items.source: Insurance Business Magazine / Gallagher Re / WTW
items.headline: Record Super El Niño Arrives as Reinsurance Property-Catastrophe Pricing Falls to Multi-Year Lows: Rates Down 16% at July 2026 Renewal; Twelve Securis Warns of Risk Redistribution Away from Atlantic Basin
items.summary: Insurance Business Magazine's October 2026 analysis highlights the structural tension between record El Niño physical risk and multi-year lows in reinsurance pricing. Property catastrophe rates fell 16% at the July 2026 midyear renewal, following a 12% drop in January — the steepest cycle downturn since 2014, per Howden Re. Swiss re-insurer Twelve Securis warned the developing super El Niño will redistribute, not reduce, risk: lower Atlantic hurricane activity may be offset by elevated typhoon (as Champi now confirms), flood, wildfire and severe weather risk globally. WTW's Torolf Hamm flagged that while direct physical damage may be adequately priced, supply-chain disruption and agricultural-income loss from climate events are systematically underpriced in current models. The Met Office projects Pacific SST anomalies exceeding 3°C later in 2026, surpassing all records since 1950.

major_events.name: Super Typhoon Champi (Western Pacific) — Re-Intensified to Super Typhoon 20 Oct; Now in Philippine PAR (Rosal); Taiwan Direct-Impact Window Confirmed 23–25 Oct; Guam Still Assessing Damage
major_events.status: As of 20 Oct morning: Champi re-intensified to super typhoon status overnight 19–20 Oct with maximum sustained winds reaching 160 mph (Category 5 equivalent) over the Philippine Sea; PAGASA confirmed entry into the Philippine Area of Responsibility and issued the local name Rosal; Signal No. 3–4 warnings may be raised for extreme northern Luzon (Batanes, Cagayan) by Tuesday. AccuWeather forecasts heavy rain and strong winds for Taiwan from Thursday night 22 Oct through Saturday 24 Oct, with up to 24 inches of rain and heaviest impacts in eastern Taiwan; Taiwan’s Central Weather Administration puts overall landfall probability at 10.9%, while ECMWF alone shows 74%. Guam, which took a direct-adjacent pass on 18 Oct, has roofs damaged, downed trees and up to 170 wells not operating — assessment ongoing.
major_events.impact: Philippines: Signal No. 3–4 wind warnings possible for extreme northern Luzon; heavy rain and flooding risk for northern and central Philippines as Champi tracks WNW; Taiwan: direct typhoon impact likely 22–25 Oct with potential 24 inches of rain, heaviest in eastern Taiwan (Hualien, Taitung window); Guam: ongoing infrastructure assessment from 18 Oct passage; forecast track uncertainty extends to southern China coast after Taiwan

major_events.name: SE Asian Haze / Indonesian Peatland Wildfires (Day 23+) — ASMC Level 3 Alert Ongoing; ASEAN Pre-Summit Enforcement Review in November
major_events.status: As of 20 Oct: ASEAN Specialised Meteorological Centre’s highest Level 3 alert remains in force; Malaysia emergency declaration still in effect for Serian Division, Sarawak; hotspot counts in Sumatra and Kalimantan remain elevated; El Niño-extended dry season continues to support fire-conducive conditions; ASEAN foreign ministers preparing to address haze enforcement at pre-summit meetings in November.
major_events.impact: Four deaths confirmed; hundreds of thousands receiving respiratory treatment across Central Kalimantan, South Sumatra and Papua; schools closed in parts of Malaysia and East Timor; Singapore legal actions against 7 identified companies ongoing

weather.overview_html: Super Typhoon Champi re-intensified overnight to Category 5-equivalent strength with 160 mph winds and entered the Philippine Area of Responsibility on 20 October — PAGASA now calls it Rosal and is preparing typhoon signal warnings for extreme northern Luzon. AccuWeather forecasts up to 24 inches of rain in eastern Taiwan from Thursday 22 October through Saturday, while Taiwan’s Central Weather Administration puts landfall probability at a more modest 10.9% (ECMWF at 74%). Guam, struck on 18 October, is still assessing infrastructure damage including 170 wells without power. Separately, the SE Asian transboundary haze crisis continues into Day 23+ under the ASMC’s highest alert. NOAA’s 15 October 2026–27 Winter Outlook confirms El Niño’s grip on the coming US winter, flagging a wet-south / warm-north pattern at >90% probability.

items.source: Philippine Star / AccuWeather / PAGASA / The Cooldown
items.headline: Super Typhoon Champi (Rosal) Re-Intensifies to Category 5 Equivalent, 160 mph Winds, Enters Philippine PAR; Taiwan Impact Window Confirmed 22–25 Oct with Up to 24 Inches Rain; Guam Damage Assessment Ongoing
items.summary: Super Typhoon Champi — assigned the local name Rosal after entering the Philippine Area of Responsibility on October 20 — re-intensified overnight to maximum sustained winds of approximately 160 mph, making it Category 5 equivalent over the Philippine Sea. PAGASA issued advisories warning that Tropical Cyclone Wind Signal No. 3 or 4 may be raised for extreme northern Luzon, including Batanes and Cagayan, by Tuesday. AccuWeather's forecast extends 24 hours of heavy rain to Taiwan from Thursday night October 22 through Saturday October 24, with rainfall potentially reaching 24 inches concentrated in eastern Taiwan. Taiwan's Central Weather Administration puts the overall landfall probability at 10.9%, while the ECMWF ensemble alone shows 74% — a large model spread reflecting genuine forecast uncertainty at this range. The storm passed approximately 10–15 miles south of Guam on October 18, ripping roofs, knocking trees and cutting power and water to as many as 170 wells; damage assessment there is still in early stages.

items.source: NOAA Climate Prediction Center / Unofficial Networks
items.headline: NOAA 2026–27 Winter Outlook Released: Super El Niño at >90% Persistence Probability Through Early Spring; Warm North / Wet South US Pattern; West Coast and Gulf States in Strongest Wet Signal; Full Detailed Outlook Due November 19
items.summary: NOAA's Climate Prediction Center released its October 2026–27 Winter Outlook on October 15, placing the probability of a strong-to-very-strong El Niño persisting through January–March 2027 above 90%. The three-month (December–February) temperature outlook favors above-normal temperatures across the northern US, Midwest and Pacific Northwest, with the southern Rockies in the 'Equal Chances' zone. Precipitation is favored above normal from Southern California and Arizona through Texas, the Gulf Coast and Southeast — the classic El Niño wet signal. Parts of the Northwest, northern Rockies and Great Lakes lean drier. The outlook explicitly notes that El Niño affects three-month averages, not individual storms, and major cold outbreaks remain possible. NOAA will release a more detailed winter outlook around November 19.

renewables.overview_html: Enel Green Power North America completed its acquisition of seven operational US solar plants (270 MW across Virginia, North Carolina and South Carolina) for approximately US$140 million on 5 October, its first entry into all three states and part of its broader 12 GW US growth target. The global offshore wind retreat continued: Equinor has cancelled the 1.2 GW Bandibuli floating offshore wind project in South Korea after losing its PPA ahead of the tender and is reviewing its entire South Korean market presence — the latest in a string of Asia-Pacific exits including Japan in June. Meanwhile, Mexico’s CFE board convened today (20 October) to vote on more than 60 solar and wind projects (8.2 GW, ~US$12.5 billion) under President Sheinbaum’s grid-reinvestment programme — the outcome of the board session is expected later today.

items.source: Renewable Watch / Mercom India / Solar Quarter
items.headline: Enel Green Power North America Completes Acquisition of Seven Operational US Solar Plants (270 MW) for ~US$140 Million; First Entry into Virginia, North Carolina and South Carolina; Adds ~0.4 TWh/yr
items.summary: Enel Green Power North America completed its acquisition of a 270 MW portfolio of seven operational solar plants across Virginia (two plants, >120 MW), North Carolina (one plant, >90 MW) and South Carolina (four plants, ~50 MW) from an unnamed US utility. The $140 million deal, originally signed in May 2026, marks Enel's first entry into all three states and is expected to generate approximately 0.4 TWh of electricity per year. Enel's group expects the acquisition to add approximately $20 million per year in ordinary EBITDA, with a ~$180 million impact on net financial debt. The acquisition is part of Enel's goal of reaching a 12 GW installed renewable capacity in the US by the end of the current strategic plan period.

items.headline: Equinor Cancels 1.2 GW Bandibuli Floating Offshore Wind (South Korea) After Losing PPA; Entire South Korean Market Presence “Under Review”; Follows Japan Exit in June
items.summary: Equinor cancelled its Bandibuli floating offshore wind project in South Korea — one of the most advanced floating wind projects in Asia at approximately 1.2 GW — after failing to secure a power purchase agreement ahead of the tender. Equinor stated it is still reviewing its offshore wind presence in South Korea and will provide an update 'at a later stage.' The company remains a partner in the Donghae 1 fixed-bottom project. The Bandibuli cancellation follows Equinor's June 2026 exit from Japan offshore wind activities and its scrapping of its 2030 renewables installed capacity target. Equinor has now materially reduced its offshore wind development footprint in South Korea, Japan, Vietnam, Spain, Portugal and France as part of a broader strategic shift toward integrated power generation.

items.source: Rio Times Online / Energy Connects / Briefs
items.headline: Mexico’s CFE Board Convenes 20 October to Vote on 60+ Solar and Wind Projects (8.2 GW, ~US$12.5 Billion); Preliminary Approval Expected; Final Contracts to Follow; Outcome Pending
items.summary: Mexico's Comisión Federal de Electricidad (CFE) board convened October 20 to vote on more than 60 renewable energy projects — primarily solar and wind — representing approximately 8.2 GW and a combined value of roughly US$12.5 billion, according to one person with knowledge of the matter. One source described the October 20 action as preliminary approval rather than final contract awarding, with the number of projects ultimately approved potentially smaller than 60. The programme is part of President Claudia Sheinbaum's strategy of enlisting private companies as CFE partners to build grid infrastructure, targeting an increase in renewables' share of generation from approximately 24% to at least 38% by 2030. Grid reliability — highlighted by seasonal blackouts in the Yucatan Peninsula — is the primary policy driver. Outcome of the October 20 board session is expected to be reported later today.

science.overview_html: Three new arXiv contributions from October 16–19 push different frontiers of AI weather research. arXiv:2610.24110 (16 Oct) applies the logit-lens “intermediate decoding” technique from language models to GraphCast, Aurora and ArchesWeather, tracking how forecast skill and physical balance evolve layer-by-layer through each model’s depth — the first mechanistic interpretability study applied systematically across multiple AI NWP architectures. arXiv:2610.26486 (19 Oct) warns that wet-biased data pipelines — where small-rain-event underreporting skews training data — systematically mislead the evaluation of generative precipitation nowcasting models, creating an apparent quality premium that disappears when bias is corrected. Meanwhile, the IJCAI 2026 paper on spherical physics-informed neural operators for downscaling introduces Spherical Laplacian Decomposition and localized integral operators that enforce dynamical consistency on a spherical grid, showing better accuracy and zero-shot generalisation to unseen query points. A fourth paper in the AIES (Vol. 5, Issue 4) from Cambridge researchers provides the first rigorous characterisation of the “effective resolution” of deterministic AI weather models, finding they track the ensemble mean across training lead times.

items.headline: arXiv:2610.24110 — Interpretability of AI Weather Models via Intermediate Decoding: Logit-Lens Applied to GraphCast, Aurora and ArchesWeather; Tracks How Physical Balance Emerges Layer-by-Layer
items.meta: Beylich & Craig (LMU Munich / ECMWF) · arXiv:2610.24110 [physics.ao-ph, cs.LG] · 16 Oct 2026
items.summary: This paper, by Matthias Beylich and George Craig (LMU Munich / ECMWF), applies the 'logit lens' or intermediate decoding technique — established in language model interpretability research — to three leading AI NWP architectures: GraphCast (Graph Neural Network), Aurora (Transformer) and ArchesWeather (Transformer). Simple linear 'translator' networks are trained to map each model's intermediate latent states into forecast-space representations, enabling layer-by-layer tracking of how forecast accuracy, spatial scale progression and physical balance constraints (geostrophy, thermal wind) build up through model depth. The analysis provides the first systematic, architecture-spanning mechanistic interpretability study for AI weather models, addressing a longstanding gap: these models can produce skilful forecasts while remaining opaque about how and where skill is generated internally. Key questions include whether physical balance conditions emerge naturally from training or are absent until the final layers, and whether different architectures converge on similar internal representations.

items.headline: arXiv:2610.26486 — Wet-Biased Data Pipelines Mislead the Training and Evaluation of Generative Precipitation Nowcasting: Apparent Quality Premium Vanishes After Bias Correction
items.summary: This preprint, submitted October 19, identifies a systematic data-quality problem affecting the evaluation of generative deep-learning precipitation nowcasting models: radar datasets commonly used for training and benchmarking exhibit a 'wet bias' caused by underreporting of very-light-rain events, which distorts both training dynamics and evaluation metrics. When models are trained on wet-biased data, they appear to achieve a premium in precipitation skill scores relative to deterministic baselines — but this apparent advantage disappears, or is substantially reduced, when the bias is corrected in the evaluation pipeline. The result calls into question published performance comparisons across several high-profile generative nowcasting systems and has direct implications for operational deployment decisions at national meteorological services. The authors provide a de-biasing methodology and show that comparative evaluations should use bias-corrected reference datasets to obtain fair assessments.

items.headline: IJCAI 2026: Spherical Physics-Informed Neural Operator with Multi-Scale Coupling for Meteorological Downscaling; Spherical Laplacian Decomposition Enforces Dynamical Consistency; Zero-Shot Generalisation to Unseen Query Points
items.meta: Yiqiang Ye et al. · IJCAI 2026, pp. 6600–6608 · arXiv:2610.24708
items.summary: This IJCAI 2026 paper (also available as arXiv:2610.24708) introduces a Spherical Physics-Informed Neural Operator (SPINO) for meteorological downscaling. The core innovation is Spherical Laplacian Decomposition, which splits atmospheric fields into frequency components on the sphere to capture both global structures and local detail — coupled with a localized spherical integral operator that queries values at arbitrary resolution grid points. Physics-informed differential constraints ensure dynamical consistency (mass conservation, divergence constraints) at the downscaled resolution. SPINO outperforms existing downscaling neural operators in accuracy benchmarks and demonstrates zero-shot generalisation to unseen query point configurations — a practical advantage for operational use at varying output resolutions without retraining. The paper connects the neural operator framework to classic spectral NWP representations, offering a theoretically grounded path toward physical consistency in learned downscaling.

items.source: Artificial Intelligence for the Earth Systems (AIES) / AMS
items.headline: AIES Vol. 5 Issue 4: “On the Effective Resolution of AI Weather Prediction Models” — Cambridge Researchers Find Deterministic AI Models Track Ensemble Mean; Implications for Skill Inflation Claims
items.meta: Selz, Allen, Bruinsma, Craig, Markou & Turner (Cambridge) · AIES Vol. 5, Issue 4, 2026
items.summary: A Cambridge-led team (Selz, Allen, Bruinsma, Craig, Markou and Turner) published a systematic study in AIES characterising the 'effective resolution' of deterministic AI weather prediction models — the spatial scale at which their output meaningfully departs from climatology and contains genuine predictive information. Their principal finding is that a perfectly trained deterministic AI weather model asymptotically tracks the mean of the forecast ensemble distribution across the lead times it was trained on, rather than providing individual ensemble member-level detail. This implies deterministic AI models suppress variability at sub-ensemble scales and cannot properly represent small-scale weather features even if they appear to produce spatially detailed output. The result provides a theoretical grounding for understanding why AI model verification scores at single deterministic runs often overstate skill relative to ensemble spread evaluations, and argues for probabilistic (ensemble) AI models as the appropriate baseline for rigorous comparison.

items.title: Rabot Energy (Germany / Benelux) Raises €50 Million Series B to Scale Residential Virtual Power Plant to One Million Customers; Endeit Capital Led; DeepTech & Climate Fonds, HV Capital, HTGF and Bosch Ventures Among Investors
items.body_html: Rabot Energy raised €50 million in a Series B round led by Endeit Capital, announced 15 October 2026, to expand its residential virtual power plant (VPP) platform to one million customers. Participating investors include the German government-backed DeepTech & Climate Fonds, HV Capital, HTGF and Bosch Ventures. Rabot’s platform aggregates home batteries, EV chargers and heat pumps, scheduling charging when renewable power is cheap and surplus electricity is abundant and discharging when demand peaks. Its Rabot Flow product, launched June 2026, bundles a dynamic tariff, smart meter and plug-in battery and claims to reduce household energy costs by approximately 15%. The company is headquartered in Hamburg and operates primarily in Germany and Benelux.

items.title: Epyr (France) Raises €15 Million Series A for Firebrick Industrial Heat Storage; SlateVC Led; First Commercial Installation Covers 25% of Steam Demand at WEPA Troyes Paper Mill; 35 MWh Unit at Papeco Next
items.body_html: Paris-based Epyr closed a €15 million Series A on 13 October, led by SlateVC, with participation from AENU, Daphni, WEPA Ventures, OVNI Capital and Aurum Impact. Founded in 2024 by Léa Dardenne and Bastien Oggeri, Epyr uses cheap or surplus electricity to heat firebricks to extreme temperatures, releasing stored heat as steam for industrial processes — decarbonising industrial heat without electrolysers or hydrogen. Its first commercial installation at WEPA Group’s Troyes paper mill now covers up to a quarter of that site’s steam needs. Proceeds will fund a 35 MWh unit at French hygiene-paper manufacturer Papeco, plus pipeline expansion across European heavy-industry customers where direct electrification is not feasible.

items.title: Record Super El Niño Meets Reinsurance Pricing Cycle Lows: Property Cat Rates Down 28% Cumulatively in 2026; Twelve Securis Warns of Risk Redistribution; Reinsurers “Nearing a Turning Point” as Physical Risk Climbs
items.body_html: Property catastrophe reinsurance rates fell 16% at the July 2026 midyear renewal (on top of a 12% January decline), the steepest combined annual slide since 2014, per Howden Re, even as the strongest El Niño since records began in 1950 was intensifying. City A.M. cites reinsurers “nearing a turning point” as physical-risk accumulation outpaces pricing correction; Gallagher Re’s Steve Bowen noted El Niño “may not bring record-breaking losses but the societal implications are considerable.” Swiss re-insurer Twelve Securis specifically warned that lower Atlantic hurricane frequency under El Niño may be more than offset by elevated typhoon, flood and wildfire exposure globally — a pattern now visible in Super Typhoon Champi, the SE Asian peatland haze and the ongoing western US fire season. The structural concern: five consecutive quarters of below-average insured losses have compressed pricing precisely as the peak El Niño heating season arrives.
